messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: privatelink-nimbus-eu-west2 egress error rate spike >60% for customer NimbusHealth. Trigger: privatelink-egress-errors > threshold. Paging on-call. (incident id PDL-3259)
ingrid_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Can someone post quick impact (APIs, DNS, latencies)?
amy_netops: looking now — grafana shows TCP retransmits + packet drop at edge -> sharp TTL variance on customer-return path. DNS query latency also elevated. https://grafana.redwood/d/privatelink/privatelink-egress (snippet)
ryan_infra: checking BGP and interfaces. show bgp neighbors summary -> neighbor 10.12.200.1 flapping, 2x BFD downs in last 5m. interface egress0 rx-errors 480/m. running tcpdump to confirm.
ryan_infra: ```
# show bgp neighbors 10.12.200.1
BGP neighbor is 10.12.200.1,  remote AS 64512
  BGP state = Established, up for 00:02:34 (flap count 3)
  Received prefixes: 128
  Last read 00:00:12, holdtime 90
# ifconfig egress0
  RX errors:480  dropped:120
```
nimbushealth_ops: we see 502/503 on our service endpoints (eu-west2) starting ~09:32UTC. Healthchecks failing intermittently. Customer impact: API calls failing for EU region users, retries incurring rate-limit hits. We're on standby.
ingrid_oncall: plan: 1) reduce traffic to problematic peering, 2) failover to backup private peering in the same region, 3) open ticket with transit provider. Amy/ryan please implement local-preference change and shift route weights. Keep customer updated.
amy_netops: applying temporary route-map to prefer backup-peering (localpref +100). Will tag routes as backup-preferred for NimbusHealth prefix set.
amy_netops: ```
route-map PREF_BACKUP permit 10
 set local-preference 200
ip prefix-list NIMBUS_PREFIX seq 5 permit 203.0.113.0/24
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.12.201.1 route-map PREF_BACKUP in
```
deploy-bot: Triggered rolling restart: privatelink-egress-proxy (eu-west2-prod) group -> rollout-id r-3259-01. Progress: 0/5
ryan_infra: quick check after route tweak: traffic shifted ~72% to backup-peering, cpu on proxies stable. error rate down from 62% -> ~12% within 2 minutes. Still seeing occasional spikes tied to flap windows.
maya_csm: FYI pinging NimbusHealth support: "We've initiated failover to backup peering and are seeing reduced errors. No expected data loss. We'll update in 10m." (sending official update)
nimbushealth_ops: thanks — seeing recovery on our side now. Any ETA on provider fix? We still see DNS TTL anomalies, our resolver cache still chasing old path occasionally.
amy_netops: opened ticket with transit provider: TICKET-PRV-98765 (severity: high). Provider notes asymmetric MPLS path possible between POP-A and POP-C, investigating. Contact: netsupport@transit.example.com, escalation id 5421.
ingrid_oncall: maintain mitigation for 30m, monitor BFD and bgp. If flaps continue, we will keep backup-preference until provider confirms stable. Also schedule postmortem after containment.
oliver_oncall: taking next shift at 10:00UTC — standby for handoff. Please DM with any outstanding actions.
ryan_infra: deploy-bot: rollout complete 5/5. proxies healthy.
amy_netops: metrics update: packet drops down 90%, TCP retrans down to baseline. DNS latencies trending down but TTL refreshes may be required at client side to clear cached bad routes.
maya_csm: sent formal customer update to NimbusHealth: "Mitigation in place, traffic shifted, provider engaged. We'll follow up with RCA and mitigation timeline." They replied :thumbsup:
ingrid_oncall: closing active paging. Monitoring window in place until 3259001850. Assigning postmortem owner: amy_netops. Please include provider comms, BGP flap root cause hypotheses, and long-term mitigations (BFD tuning, route dampening thresholds).
amy_netops: acknowledged. I'll open postmortem doc and link when ready. :white_check_mark:
pagerbot: Incident resolved (PDL-3259) — error rates returned to baseline, customer confirmed recovery. Closing alert at 3259001850.
summary: Privatelink egress multipath jitter caused BGP flaps and DNS TTL anomalies; traffic failed over to backup peering, provider engaged, containment achieved, postmortem assigned
